We're scared of the Xenomorphs again, but Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 knows old-fashioned bug hunts shouldn't be a thing of the past.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games, and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel.

At Summer Game Fest 2026, we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong?

Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years.

Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2's pure survival horror to look forward to.

Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason.

Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat.

This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running.

All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode.

At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away.

There are still some scares hiding in here, though, ready to make complacent players jump out of their seats. Special Xenomorphs have tricks to pounce on distracted players, throwing chaos into the middle of their carefully coordinated rain of fire. Others have the ability to spit from afar, breaking tight defenses that count on the Xenos' predictable tactics from other games and the movies.

It's been 40 years since Aliens first graced the big screen, but Fireteam Elite 2 manages to refresh that mix of horror and action well enough, despite sharing much of its bones with the original game. But the disturbing lack of polish threatens to undo Cold Iron Studios' best ideas.

Those ideas include more varied enemies, which can disrupt almost any tried-and-tested team composition, and even a late-game class that rewards an extensive knowledge of the game by letting veterans pick weapons from all over the roster to create a custom loadout.

These playful creative swings somewhat offset the frustration caused by glitched objectives, enemy AI that often goes off the rails, and performance issues that have often given me flashbacks to its predecessor's worst moments on PS4. Sometimes, you can just tell when six extra months would've done a game a lot of good, and it's obvious that Fireteam Elite 2 will be in a much better place by spring.

That said, its loose and confident approach to design is rare to see when dealing with games that adapt well-established IPs like Alien.

Recent Star Wars games have achieved just that, and even if Fireteam Elite 2 misses some of its shots and has faced more initial trouble than the USCM's first incursion on LV-426, it's safe to say its heart and mind are in the right place. No one can take that away from the devs. Show me another modern Alien video game that allows you to zap Xenomorphs to death with a big cannon or to hold them off with combat drones.

We've seen developers win uphill battles before, and we know for a fact the huge Alien fandom is as enduring as the deadly extraterrestrials, so Daybreak and Cold Iron have a chance to turn things around and solidify Fireteam Elite 2 as the iterative but satisfying sequel it actually is.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is available now for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. A Nintendo Switch 2 version is coming in 2027.

#837. Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows

Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," said the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons."

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

The study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters said. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%."

It is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

While the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

And even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

#836. Bellamy convinced of Wales credentials despite defeat by Portugal

Craig Bellamy's Wales seriously tested reigning Nations League champions Portugal in Cardiff

Craig Bellamy kept coming back to one word. Belief.

His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised.

But there are ways of losing and ways of finishing bottom.

Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff.

And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances mean they at least have the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status.

"Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign.

"Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level.

"We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop.

"You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift."

Portugal hold off bold Wales in five-goal thriller

Former Wales captain Craig Bellamy was appointed head coach in July 2024

Wales have certainly fared better than they did when they were last in the top tier of the Nations League, when they finished with one point from six games and were relegated.

Victory against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway last month was their first at this level and, had they been more clinical in Oslo on Saturday, they might have got a second win of the campaign.

Ultimately, Wales' inability to take their chances â combined with sloppy defensive mistakes â meant their results did not match their performances.

And the reality is that they were up against stellar opposition, whose vastly superior resources showed with their greater ruthlessness at both ends of the pitch.

"If there's anything you would have learned from these games, then you see killers. That's why they're at the top," Bellamy added.

"I know people look at results. I'm fully aware of the business. This is all I know. But I think when you look at reality as well, and you look at our performances during this group, I couldn't ask for more.

"I feel we're closer than probably maybe the players thought they were. It's fine margins.

"But I feel the biggest word out of this now has been belief, really, for me."

Highlights: 10-man Portugal defeat Wales to top Nations League group

Wales had the best record of the four teams who finished bottom of their top-flight groups, meaning they have a second chance to avoid relegation in the form of a two-leg play-off in March.

At Friday's draw in Switzerland, Bellamy's side will discover whether they will face Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia-Herzegovina, who beat them in a World Cup play-off earlier this year.

Those teams all finished second in their League B groups and, as the League A team, Wales will have home advantage in the second leg.

"Going into the next one, we have to be in this group," said Bellamy. "If we want to develop as a football nation and keep going forward, we have to be playing against the best teams. It's only going to improve you.

"I know we can go back to League B... It's about playing the best teams. That's how we're going to get better. I honestly believe it."

Bellamy, who has a contract running to 2028, said: "I won't be here for the next Nations League. I won't be the manager then. So I'm doing it for the next one, but I'm also doing it for the players.

"We've got to. That's how we're going to be the best version of us and keep improving."

#835. Joe Jonas Reveals Cheeky Gift He Recently Gave Ex Demi Lovato

Joe Jonas recently revealed that he gave Demi Lovato, whom he dated briefly in 2010, a cheeky birthday gift that nodded toward one of her most viral interview moments.

Joe Jonas’ favorite meme? He would have to say mug.

More than 10 years after Demi Lovato went viral for revealing mugs were her “favorite dish” during an interview with NRJ Berlin, her Camp Rock costar—whom she dated briefly in 2010—revealed it’s still his favorite pop culture moment.

“It’s amazing,” Joe told his brothers Kevin Jonas and Nick Jonas during the Nov. 17 episode of their Hey Jonas! podcast. “I bought her a mug as a gift for coming as our special guest recently or her birthday. I think I sent her a mug for her birthday. I can’t remember.”

Meanwhile, Kevin and Joe agreed it was a great clip.  As Kevin emphasized, “She wasn’t incorrect.”

For Demi’s part, she recently revealed that she intentionally had misinterpreted the question—the interviewer was referring to food rather than cookware—but she opted to answer it in her own way.

“I had been asked so many questions that day,” Demi reflected during an appearance on Keke Palmer’s Baby, It’s Keke Palmer podcast in March. “I was doing, like, a press tour and you get bored doing press tours.”

And so, the Disney Channel alum joked she thought at the time, “‘I’m gonna start f--king with the interviewers.’”

“I just ran with it,” Demi joked, emphasizing that only part of the interview went viral. “In the long, extended video, you see me look at my tour manager and like smirk. Like, ‘did you catch that one?’ And then that went viral and everyone thought I was serious.”

But there’s nothing wrong with being confident in answering the question this way, especially given Demi made a worthy case for mugs.

“I like mugs because they’re very comfortable in your hand,” she said in the now-viral clip. “And they hold hot things that you don’t have to touch. So, you know, coffee or hot tea.”

As for Joe running so far with the joke that he sent his ex a mug as a present? While Demi previously joked she was “mad” at Joe following their breakup, there’s no longer any mean mugging between them.

“It’s been such a wonderful relationship through so many years,” Joe told USA Today earlier this year after he and Demi each made appearances at each other’s respective concerts. “I feel so grateful that Demi and I can go perform together still and see each other in these different journeys of our life.”

For more Disney alums who dated, keep reading…

Disney Channel worlds collided after Sabrina Carpenter met Bradley Steven Perry.

The Girl Meets World star and Good Luck Charlie actor’s romance began in 2014, when Carpenter’s show began filming right next door to Perry’s Mighty Med.

“[It was a] really unique way to ask someone out,” Carpenter told J-14 at the time, describing a scene out of a pirate flick: “Like, they do the little bottles and they put notes in them and send them across the ocean, like one of those, and [he] put a note inside. It was cute.”

Though they broke up in 2015, Perry—who married Candace Cameron Bure’s daughter Natasha Bure in 2025—noted that their connection was a sweet young love.

“Sabrina was my first girlfriend,” Perry said during an appearance on the Unplanned Podcast in 2024. “We dated for about two years.”

He added, “It was very much like a little high school relationship.”

Bella Thorne and Gregg Sulkin shook up young Hollywood when they first stepped out together in 2015.

But the Shake It Up alum and Wizards of Waverly Place actor went their separate ways a year later.

“Our schedules made seeing each other difficult," Thorne and Sulkin told People in a joint statement back in 2016, “and we decided that for now this would be best.”

But they’ll always look back on their fairytale romance with a smile.

“After much thought and soul-searching, we have made the difficult decision to end our relationship,” they added. “We will always love each other and have a deep respect for one another, as we have each grown to be better people because of our time together.”

Can you imagine what would happen if Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens never dated?

The High School Musical alums hit it off as soon as the cameras started rolling for the franchise’s first film in 2005.

“We created a bond right from the start,” Hudgens—who played the Gabriella Montez to Efron’s Troy Bolton in the films—told People in 2022. “We were like, ‘We’re doing this, it’s us or nothing.’”

“It started off really organically,” she added. “I could not have been more grateful to have that relationship at that time.”

And while the pair eventually had to go their own ways, you can still bet on the fact that they had a next-level connection.

As Hudgens put it on a 2025 episode of Bart Johnson's Get Your Head In The Game podcast, "Of course I was a child and paired with this boy and I was like, 'Oh my god, he's so cute.' The chemistry was so real."

Nick Jonas and Selena Gomez’s romance was burnin’ up from 2008 to 2010.

And while they shared two years together, Gomez’s real prize from the relationship would have to be her unbreakable bond with BFF Taylor Swift.”

“Taylor and I dated the Jonas Brothers,” Gomez—who married Benny Blanco in 2025—said during a 2025 episode of the Therapuss with Jake Shane podcast of how she and Swift met. “I dated Nick and she dated Joe [Jonas]. And everything  was cute, we were young. We all know and love each other now and it’s so cute.”

Gomez added of her relationship with Jonas, dad to daughter Malti with wife Priyanka Chopra, “She and I like to say the best thing we got out of those relationships was each other because it was really sweet.”

At one point, Miley Cyrus thought Dylan Sprouse could be the one.

Indeed, the Hannah Montana alum revealed she and The Suite Life of Zack & Cody star were much more than work colleagues.

“Dylan Sprouse was my boyfriend,” Cyrus told Alex Cooper during the March 2026 Disney+ Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special. “I think he was the cutest.”

Responding to past rumors that she and Sprouse—who married model Barbara Palvin in 2023—were an item, the “Flowers” singer added, “It's true, confirmed.”

But during their brief romance, she also got to spend quality time with Sprouse’s twin brother Cole Sprouse—though she knew she couldn’t have the best of both worlds.

“Dylan was my crush,” Cyrus continued. “Their dad would take us to sushi. I was into the whole culture, and it was a two-for-one. Like, bring the brother. Hello!”

Joe Jonas and Demi Lovato may be like Venus and Mars, but they were once on the same astral plane.

After all, the Camp Rock alums took their romance offscreen in 2010 while filming the film’s sequel, though they backed down from the connection about a year later.

“Demi and I knew going into our romantic relationship that it may not be an easy one,” Jonas told Us Weekly in 2025. “I realize over the time we have shared together that I feel I care more about our friendship right now.”

That’s why the Jonas Brothers member wouldn’t change a thing about the love story he shared with Lovato—who married Jordan “Jutes” Lutes in 2025.

“It was my choice to break up,” Jonas—who shares daughters Willa and Delphine with ex-wife Sophie Turner—added, “but I love her as a friend. She’s been there for me when I needed her. I will continue to be her friend and be there for her.”

Revisiting Assumptions About Extraterrestrial Life

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Episode 236 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize.

When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms.

But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.
